It was my first week working in the mobile department of a large electronics retailer. I fit in pretty well with my co-workers and manager (still talk to them all semi-daily). 

I'll always remember this customer as the cowboy. He was probably around 6'3, 6'4, very pale wearing sunglasses and a cowboy hat on top of his balding head. He strolled in and walked to the front of a decently long line (it's the week of a major shopping event, there was a pretty long line). He then proceeded to tell me he wanted the latest model of a popular smartphone that had come out about a month prior for a major carrier. 

I told him he would have to wait in line, and that we were out of the phone he wanted. He complained for about 10 minutes about the customer experience and how I was a poor employee. He then asked me if it was my first day. I let him know it was my fifth and his face turned bright red. After a few more choice words to me, he asked me what I was going to do to redeem myself from the situation. I told him I refused to have this conversation anymore, and that he needed to proceed to the back of the line if he wanted service. He let out a soft insult and proceeded to the back of the line. 

About 45 minutes later he had made it to the front of the line and two coworkers were finished with their customers and they both asked him if he needed service. He told them he was waiting for me. Admittedly I took my time with the customer, a mix of me being new and it being multiple upgrades made it believable. 

He walked up, plopped down on the bench and said, "now give me the phone, and I want a discount on my bill or I'll have a word with your manager." I asked what he wanted and he repeated the phone from earlier. I told him we hadn't received a phone shipment in the past hour, and he would have to pick another phone. He then proceeded to scream at me at the top of his lungs, saying that I told him I would hold the phone for him and that I was a liar and a fool. 

At this point I'm sort of laughing in my head, trying not to smirk. I'm pretty good under pressure, and went the first 17 years of my life being screamed at, so this was almost comical. 

Finally after settling down a bit he decided on a different phone we did have in stock. I pulled it out and looked up his account. And pure bliss enveloped over me. His bill was going to rise either $25 with a $400 down payment, or rise $35.42 with an $80 down payment. I told him the bad news and he burst. Told me to get my manager, this is ridiculous, worst customer service he had ever received, and I was a fool. That was his favorite word. My manager walked over, asked the problem, the guy demanded a free phone on the house from the retailer or he would call corporate, yada yada yada. 

Finally I was fed up. I looked at my manager and he said "do you have some input on this?" 

I said yes. Turned to the man. Told him he wouldn't be getting a free phone and to leave. 

My manager immediately told me to go to the back room. I waited in there about 20 minutes. My manager came in. He told me that the customer complained to him for 20 minutes, and my manager told me that I would be dealt with accordingly. 

I went from part time to full time that day. My manager thought it was hilarious. He said that guy had been coming in every couple of months to yell about stuff. We never saw him again. I love that job because of my boss. Miss him every day. You're my boy!
